chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever has a share of harshness (in his behaviour), the Emān is separated from him.

key_terms.الْخُرْقُ: Harshness, awkwardness, or lack of ease in manners and behavior
key_terms.حُجِبَ: Separated, veiled, or prevented from reaching

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of harshness in manners on a person's faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, 'khurq' (harshness or awkwardness) is interpreted not merely as social clumsiness but as a spiritual rigidity that obstructs the heart's receptivity to divine grace. This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights that while faith (iman) encompasses belief, its perfection is contingent upon refined character (akhlaq), linking the internal state of faith directly to external conduct. The hadith serves as a warning that a lack of ease in dealings with others indicates a deficiency in one's spiritual connection.
